BIYAHENG PINOY DILG Legal Opinion No. 63 s. 2 11 OCT 18 2011 DIR. PEDRO A. NOVAL, JR. Regional Director DILG Regional Office No. VII Sudlon, Lahug, Cebu City Dear Reg. Director Pedro A. Noval, Jr.: This has reference to your letter wherein you seek a definitive ruling from this Department on whether Regional Order No. 2010-010, as amended by Regional Order No. 2010-010A pertaining to the reassigment/designation of Josefina Daisy S. Cabo as LGRC/Call Center Administrator are legal. We are aware that the issuance of Regional Order No. 2010-010 (later on amended by Regional Order No. 2010-010A) pertaining to the reassigment/designation of Josefina Daisy S. Cabo of the Regional Office No. VII as LGRC/Call Center Administrator, which is the subject of this query, is the same issue raised by Ms. Cabo causing the latter to file a civil suit for damages against you on 11 March 2010 before the Regional Trial Court of Cebu, Branch 8, Cebu City. Said case is still pending even as of this writing. The sub judice rule restricts comments and disclosures pertaining to judicial proceedings to avoid prejudging the issue, influencing the court, or obstructing the administration of justice. A violation of the sub judice rule may render one liable for indirect contempt under Sec. 3(d), Rule 71 of the Rules of Court. (Rhegis M. Romero rx, et al. vs Sen. -Jinggoy Ejercito Estrada, G.R. No. 174105, 02 April 2009) The requested opinion on whether the Regional Orders you issued is intimately related to the issues for determination by the Court and may traverse the same, and for this Office to issue a legal opinion thereon may be deemed a violation of the subjudice rule, unnecessarily exposing the Department to an indirect contempt by the Court. However, by way of reiteration, please be guided by the previous issuances and communication from this Department, particularly the letter dated 12 March 2010 wherein this Office, without knowledge and unaware of any suit filed against you, cited Circular No. 2007-09 (Tab "F") which amended DILG Circular No. 99-18 dated 01 June 1999 on the Comprehensive Delegation of Authority which reads: "xx the Undersecretary for Local Government shall act on all requests for movement, transfer and reassignment of field personnel (LG Sector) from the rank of Assistant Division Chief or its equivalent (LGOO VII) and below. xxx AI/ Regional Director, BFP and BJMP Assistant Regional Director and PPSC Regional Training Director shall act, sign and /or approve the transfer/reassignment or detail

of personel below Section Chief and Inspector levels within the region. " The circulars issued by the Department are couched in clear and simple language, and easily understandable, leaving no room for interpretation. Even if one interprets the foregoing statements, the same should be take in their natural, plain, and ordinary acceptation and signification. Thus, for purposes of clarifying the policies set forth under Circular No. 99-18, as amended by Circular No. 2007-09, the Undersecretary for Local Government is authorized to act on all requests for movement, transfer and reassignment of field personnel (LG Sector) from the rank of Assistant Division Chief or its equivalent (LGOO VI) and below . The positions covered by the word "below", over which the Undersecretary for Local Government has authority, refer to those that are lower than the rank of an Assistant Division Chief or its equivalent. Circular No. 2007-09, however, did not repeal the prior circular on comprehensive delineation of authority, that is, Circular No. 99-18 dated 01 June 1999, as the amendment pertained only to the movement, transfer and reassignment of field personnel (LG Sector), thus, the authority delineated under the earlier circular which are not inconsistent to the latter issuance remain in full force and effect. In fact, in his Memorandum dated 17 March 2010 addressed to your goodself, Usec. Austere A. Panadero stated that "field offices pertain to provincial, city, and municipal levels as distinguished from the regional office proper". A final word to put the issue to rest while the Regional Directors exercise a delineated authority on specific transactions concerning their respective regions, the Secretary and his Undersecretaries are not precluded from exercising similar authority that they themselves delegated and from which the delegated authority transcended, as it is within the mandate of their respective offices to perform such. Very truly yours, A . JESUS Director III LS:55/06 .D UE lv
